title: Ocean currents and temperature, 2007 to 2008
summary: Thirty world maps, eleven days apart from March 2007 to February 2008, of the ocean surface currents drawn as streaks coloured by sea surface temperature, from blue (0 degrees Celsius) to red (32).
description: Ocean surface currents from the ECCO2 ocean model (NASA/JPL and MIT), drawn by NASA's Scientific Visualization Studio as streaks that follow the flow, coloured by sea surface temperature on a scale from 0 degrees Celsius (blue) through green and yellow to 32 (red). ECCO2 is a computer model that takes in measurements from satellites and from the sea; it is not a direct measurement. In NASA's pictures the streaks are shaded darker for a three-dimensional look, which hides their colour from the app. So for this data set each clearly coloured streak pixel was brightened back to full strength and matched to the nearest colour on NASA's colour bar, and each map was made half size by keeping, around each point, the streak pixel that best matches the bar. Land (grey) and the black background are not changed and count as no data. The thin streaks leave gaps, so only about a third of each map is read, most of it in the tropics and mid-latitudes; the cold polar seas are drawn dark and are read least. The numbers are read from the colours, so they are about, not exact.

source.name: NASA Scientific Visualization Studio, Global Sea Surface Currents and Temperature (ECCO2 model, NASA/JPL and MIT)
source.credit: NASA/Goddard Space Flight Center Scientific Visualization Studio. Animators: Greg Shirah (NASA/GSFC), Horace Mitchell (NASA/GSFC), Eric Sokolowsky (Global Science and Technology, Inc.). Scientists: Hong Zhang (UCLA), Dimitris Menemenlis (NASA/JPL CalTech). Data: ECCO2 (NASA/JPL); topography: GTOPO30 (USGS).

regions.description: The whole map; land and the gaps between streaks count as no data.
